# required-checks.txt — the manifest `ci-required` reads (ADR-002 § CI fan-in).
#
# One check name per line. `ci-required` collects the result of every name here
# and FAILS on anything other than success: failure, cancellation, timeout,
# SKIP, or never having run. A skipped required lane is not a pass
# (AGENTS.md).
#
# This file and the workflows are CODEOWNERS-protected: a PR that edits the gate
# it is gated by needs owner review (ADR-002 § Branch protection, item 7).
#
# scripts/ci-required-guard.sh additionally enforces a FLOOR: the lanes listed
# in its FLOOR_LANES array must be present here and must not be marked optional.
# Deleting a required line therefore turns the guard red with a named error,
# rather than quietly shrinking the gate — see
# docs/evidence/warroom/2026-09-20-vizra-user-pr1-skeleton-SECURITY.md Finding 2.

append-only
build-test
cache-matrix
fixtures
govulncheck
docker-build

# DELIBERATELY ABSENT: image-scan.yml's `image-scan`.
#
# Not an oversight and not a dodge. The guard forbids `continue-on-error` on a
# floor lane on purpose — a lane that hides its own failures is worse than no
# lane — but a vulnerability scan's result depends on the WORLD: a CVE published
# against an unfixed Debian package turns it red with no change to this
# repository, and a required lane that goes red on its own is how a team learns
# to merge past red.
#
# So it runs on every pull request, fails loudly, publishes its report, and is
# read by a human. Promoting it is an owner-reviewed change to BOTH this file
# and FLOOR_LANES in scripts/ci-required-guard.py, and that PR should carry a
# baseline that has been clean for a sustained period and an agreed route for an
# unfixed upstream CVE — a reviewed, expiring .trivyignore.yaml entry — so that
# "red for reasons outside the repository" has an answer that is not
# continue-on-error.
#
# Its own anti-vacuity controls do not depend on being required: see
# scripts/image-scan-verdict.py and scripts/testdata/imagescan/.
